text: Standard single-mode fiber (SMF-28) has its zero-dispersion wavelength near 1310 nm, yet long-haul systems operate at 1550 nm. What is the chromatic dispersion of SMF-28 at 1550 nm?
explanation: SMF-28 exhibits about +17 ps/(nm*km) of anomalous chromatic dispersion at 1550 nm. 0 ps/(nm*km) confuses 1550 nm with the zero-dispersion wavelength (1310 nm); -17 has the wrong sign (that regime lies below the zero-dispersion wavelength); 0.18 confuses dispersion with the fiber's loss figure of 0.18 dB/km.
